newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH TRUCK MAKER REVERSES YEARS OF LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TRUCK MAKER REVERSES YEARS OF LOSSES.

text.p: Troubled Czech truck maker Tatra a.s., controlled by engineering concern Skoda a.s. , on Thursday said it had reversed years of losses in 1996, closing the year with a "balanced performance".
Company spokesman Ivo Celachovsky would not give further details on the firm's 1996 financial results, after stating earlier this month that Tatra would end 1996 with a loss.
"In November and December...a turn in production occured, resulting into a balanced performance and getting some orders for 1997, which will fill the capacity of the company," Celachovsky said.
He said Tatra is forecasting a 70 million crown profit in 1997, with production nearly doubling to 3,200 trucks from 1,804 in 1996.
"The supervisory board consider a 100 increase in turnover in 1997 as realistic," he added.

Tatra used to make up to 15,000 heavy duty trucks per year at its peak before the end of socialism in 1989, but production has fallen to a fraction of communist-era levels after disintegration of eastern markets.
Tatra, 43 percent owned by Skoda which also controls long-haul truck producer Liaz , recorded a consolidated loss of 775 million crowns in 1995.
Skoda has revealed a plan to start production of Detroit Diesel Corp engines at Tatra's plant.
